title: Femoral Triangle: Boundaries, Contents and Clinical Access
subject: Anatomy
preview: The femoral triangle is bounded superiorly by the inguinal ligament, laterally by sartorius and medially by adductor longus.
quickRevision: The femoral triangle is bounded superiorly by the inguinal ligament, laterally by sartorius and medially by adductor longus.
The femoral sheath encloses vessels but not the femoral nerve.
Femoral vascular access requires ultrasound and careful distinction of artery and vein where available.

sections.title: Core biomedical mechanism
points: The femoral triangle is bounded superiorly by the inguinal ligament, laterally by sartorius and medially by adductor longus.
From lateral to medial, the usual relationship is femoral nerve, artery, vein and lymphatic space.

sections.title: Clinical application
points: The femoral sheath encloses vessels but not the femoral nerve.
Femoral vascular access requires ultrasound and careful distinction of artery and vein where available.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: The femoral nerve lies outside the femoral sheath despite being within the triangle.
